name: Starter: Luxembourgish
about: Luxembourgish in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Luxembourgish order.

words.du: you (to a friend; dech: you as the object)
words.sinn: be (ass: is; si before most consonants)
words.mäin: my (meng: feminine and plural; mäi before most consonants)
words.hunn: have (hues: you have, huet: has; hu before most consonants)
words.keen: no, not a (keng: feminine and plural; kee before most consonants)
words.Dir: you (polite, to one or more people)
words.eisen: our (eis with a feminine or plural noun)
words.ginn: give (et gëtt: there is, there are)
words.fueren: go (by car, bus, train or bike), drive
words.entschëllegen: excuse (Entschëllegt: excuse me, to someone you call Dir)

items.text: En Téi an e Waasser, wannechgelift.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Eng Téi an e Waasser, wannechgelift.
En Téi an eng Waasser, wannechgelift.
Jo, mir et gutt, merci. Äddi!
Nee, mir et gutt, merci. Äddi!

wrong: Ech hues e Brudder an eng Schwëster.
Ech hunn eng Brudder an e Schwëster.

Ech wunnen an e klengen Haus.

items.means: My mother goes to the city.
Tomorrow I'm going to the city.

items.means: The cat sleeps on my bed.

concept.line: Most verbs end in -en with ech, mir and si (they), -s with du and -t with hien, si (she) and Dir: ech wunnen, du wunns, hie wunnt, mir wunnen.
In a yes-or-no question the verb comes first; after a question word, it comes next: Wou wunns du?

words.means: hunn = have; hues = have; hu = have

concept.line: Articles, pronouns, verb forms and most words ending in -en drop their final n (both letters of -nn) before most consonants, and keep it before a vowel, d, h, n, t or z, and before sentence punctuation or a slash; with a hyphen or an opening quotation mark between, the next word decides: den Hond but de Bus, ech drénke Kaffi but ech drénken Téi, mir si fort but mir sinn do.
Every noun is masculine, feminine or neuter.
my is mäin with a masculine or neuter noun (mäi before most consonants, by the n-rule) and meng with a feminine or plural one: mäi Papp (my dad), meng Mamm (my mom), meng Schlësselen (my keys).

words.means: ginn = go; gees = go; geet = goes

concept.line: In a statement the verb comes second.
